stories.title: Brock Purdy needs help. Winners and losers from 49ers' loss to Falcons
stories.summary: The 49ers perfect start to the season is over thanks to the Falcons. But at least Christian McCaffrey's injury doesn't appear to be serious.
stories.detailText: ATLANTA – So much for a perfect season. The San Francisco 49ers coughed up four turnovers and fell from the ranks of the NFL’s undefeated team on Sunday, falling 29-20 to the Atlanta Falcons . Six days after surviving a furious rally by the Commanders on Monday night, the injury-ravaged 49ers (6-1) lost star running back Christian McCaffrey for much of the first half due to a thigh injury and couldn’t hang on to an early 11-point lead. Atlanta (3-4) stormed back after McCaffrey’s fill-in, Kaelon Black, fumbled away a scoring opportunity in the third quarter. Rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels had a huge role in finishing off the 49ers, collecting an interception and fumble recovery in the fourth quarter. Winners and losers: WINNERS Kendal Daniels A week after being strapped to a stretcher and carted off the field in a scary scene , then taken to nearby Grady Hospital for a neck injury, the rookie linebacker was the first Falcons player announced to the crowd for pre-game introductions. Fitting. Then Daniels left a major mark on the game’s result with a spectacular interception and 29-yard return in the fourth quarter that set up a field goal that gave Atlanta a two-possession cushion. And he finished the day with the recovery of a George Kittle fumble in the final minute. Kevin Stefanski It would have been so embarrassing if the first-year Falcons coach wound up on the losing end when matched against his predecessor, new 49ers defensive coordinator Raheem Morris. Well, thanks to his defense – coordinated by Jeff Ulbrich – forcing a season-high four turnovers, Stefanski wound up in the winner’s circle. Jesse Bates III The wily Falcons safety had fingerprints on two of the turnovers, with a diving interception and forced fumble that clearly made a big difference. Christian McCaffrey San Francisco’s dynamic running back missed much of the first half after suffering a thigh injury. But he still produced 100 yards from scrimmage, with 39 yards rushing and 61 receiving on six catches. It’s too bad the injury disrupted his flow as CMC started so well to power a game-opening drive that he capped with a 1-yard TD dive. Za’Darius Smith The 12 th -year veteran, a much-needed piece for the Falcons given the absence of second-year edge rushers James Pearce Jr. (suspension) and Jalon Walker (torn ACL), collected a huge fourth-down sack of Brock Purdy with the 49ers furiously trying to cash in while in scoring range in the fourth quarter. It was also the first sack given up this season by San Francisco’s All-World left tackle Trent Williams, which makes it doubly impressive. Tight Ends They were all over the place. Falcons backup Nick Muse scored his first NFL touchdown in the first half, wide open on first-and-goal from the 1. Kyle Pitts gave Atlanta its first lead with a 5-yard TD to open the second half. Charlie Woerner took a direct snap and converted a third-and-short into a first down. On the 49ers ledger, Luke Farrell recovered a fumble. George Kittle had a team-high eight receptions for 88 yards. And in the Fox broadcast booth, Greg Olsen brought deft insight, as usual. All on “National Tight Ends Day” at that. LOSERS 49ers Infirmary As if the 49ers don’t already resemble a M*A*S*H unit with such a lengthy injury list, San Francisco lost McCaffrey after their opening series with a thigh injury. He missed the remainder of the first half but was able to return after halftime. This for a team playing without defensive end Nick Bosa and devastated by injuries to its wide receivers corps, with Mike Evans (Achilles) on Sunday joining the list of missing wideouts that includes Deebo Samuael, Christian Kirk, Ricky Pearsall, Demarcus Robinson and impressive rookie De’Zhaun Stribling. Brock Purdy Did we mention the 49ers are down on their luck with receivers? That surely makes it tough on the 49ers quarterback, who had a rough one without his most established wideouts and threw two interceptions for the first time all season – which matched his season total for picks heading into the game. Raheem Morris Unceremoniously dumped in January after just two seasons as Falcons head coach, Morris has landed as 49ers defensive coordinator and returned to the ATL with an undefeated team and a chance to deliver some payback. If only it turned out that way. Kickers on PATs No, it’s not automatic. Especially for 49ers kicker Eddie Piniero, who missed his fourth extra-point kick of the season as San Francisco mounted a rally in the fourth quarter. Nick Folk missed one for the Falcons, too, early in the game…and it was his first miss of the season. ATL’s homefield advantage Sure, they can “Swag Surf” with the best of them at the festive atmosphere of Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Yet once again it was tough to figure out which was the “home” team as 49er fans showed up en masse – aided, of course, by the Falcons season ticket holders willing to sell their seats. stories.title: Packers' top two centers are questionable to return
stories.summary: Packers running back Josh Jacobs' first carry of the season has taken center Sean Rhyan off the field.
stories.detailText: Packers running back Josh Jacobs' first carry of the season has taken center Sean Rhyan off the field. Jacobs and Lions edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson rolled over Rhyan's left ankle from behind. The Packers list Rhyan as questionable to return with an ankle injury. Jacob Monk, who lost his starting right guard job after three games, replaced Rhyan at center. But he didn't last long, leaving with a quadriceps injury. Monk, too, is questionable to return. John Williams went in at center for the Packers' second series. Williams had not previously snapped in any game, including the preseason. The Packers did just fine, driving 74 yards in 12 plays to tie the game 7-7 on Tucker Kraft's 14-yard reception from Jordan Love. Love is 10-of-14 for 122 yards and a touchdown. The Packers should have scored on their first possession, but rookie Trey Smack missed a 26-yard field goal.

stories.title: Aaron Glenn 'highly disappointed' after loss to Dolphins, but believes Jets are 'on the right track'
stories.summary: Head coach Aaron Glenn takes accountability for the Jets' home loss to the Miami Dolphins, but maintains that his team is "on the right track".
stories.detailText: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn is taking the blame for the team's 28-25 home loss at the hands of a dismal divisional foe, the Miami Dolphins . "Highly disappointed, disappointed in myself, first and foremost," said Glenn as he began his postgame press conference. "We all have to get better. From coaching, to playing, to everything we're doing, we have to get better," he continued. Glenn then looked ahead, urging his 2-5 squad to rally around both him and each other to make the most of a season that is seemingly slipping away. "The thing is, this is seven games. We still have a number of games left, and that's how we look at it," he asserted. "It is what it is. This is the time for our guys to lock arms and make sure that everything we get as far as energy and connection is built from within." One key drive from the game which stood out to Glenn upon reflection was Miami's final drive of the second quarter. The Dolphins began that drive with 8:44 left in the quarter from their own nine yard line, and drove the entire 91 yards on 15 plays to extend their lead to 21-7, leaving the Jets with just six seconds remaining in the first half. "Maybe we should've called our timeouts to get it back, but at that point, we just felt like we were going to stop them and be able to get the ball back," Glenn explained. His defense allowed 28 points, plus a failure to stop the Dolphins from running out the clock at the end of the game, which was 'really puzzling' to the head coach. "Defensively, we have to do a better job," Glenn declared. "We've got to play better. Our fans deserve better than that, and that starts with me, so I'm going to make sure I'm going everything I can to get our guys ready for our next game." Finally, Glenn was asked if he feels the Jets are headed in the right direction. "I would say yes, because there's no quit in these guys," he concluded. "Listen, I know what the record is, I do, but I also know what I feel about these players and how they play." "I know that we're not where we need to be. But I totally believe that we're on the right track."

stories.title: Week 7 snap reactions: Falcons fight off their demons and finish
stories.summary: Atlanta’s effort was uneven but they got the job done in sensational fashion against the 49ers.
stories.detailText: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 25: Nick Muse #87 of the Atlanta Falcons reacts after a touchdown reception during the second quarter against the San Francisco 49ers at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Atlanta Falcons finally won a home game, and they did it the only way they know how, by giving you a heart attack. Here are the Week 7 snap reactions. Week 7: Atlanta Falcons vs San Francisco 49ers https://t.co/bunziB0sVH pic.twitter.com/DnGiWeIXbx — Tre’Shon (@tre3shon) October 25, 2026 National Tight Ends Day Tommy Rees celebrated the occasion by getting his tight ends involved; every one on the active roster finished the game with at least one catch. Kyle Pitts led the way, scoring another touchdown and marking three straight games with at least one. Nick Muse came in with one career catch and left with two and a touchdown, and Austin Hooper and Charlie Woerner got active to the tune of 3 receptions for 30 yards. We’ve been waiting for Rees to lean on his tight ends more, and we were rewarded. Every day should be Tight Ends Day for this offense. Welcome to the National Tight Ends Day touchdown party, @kylepitts__ SFvsATL on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/xisNvvBH2q — NFL (@NFL) October 25, 2026 Defense holds off the comeback The 49ers moved the ball well in the second half, but two critical defensive stops saved the day. With their backs up against their own end zone, the Falcons prevented the 49ers from scoring and sacked Brock Purdy on 4th down . Later, after the Falcons offense went three-and-out again, rookie LB Kendal Daniels turned the tide with a sensational interception, shutting down the 49ers comeback hopes. He later scooped up a fumble caused by Jessie Bates III, officially ending the game. The defense forced four turnovers today, and that was the difference. It wasn’t always pretty, but the defense got it done when it mattered most. @AtlantaFalcons rookie Kendal Daniels gets his first career interception in the clutch SFvsATL on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/9BtAUNZQLm — NFL (@NFL) October 25, 2026 Special Teams still killing the team The opening return from Branch was great to see, but I think I speak for everyone when I say it’s getting exhausting watching this unit play bad football. Teams are almost guaranteed to start with the ball on the 35, and after having little issue on the punt team, Jake Bailey shanked a punt at the worst possible moment. Nick Folk missing an extra point attempt was the cherry on top. Luckily, the offense and defense carried the load today, but this unit keeps making costly mistakes week in and week out. Michael Penix Jr. is growing In back-to-back weeks, Penix has thrown three touchdowns and zero interceptions; this was the third such game of his career, and the first in a win. Growth isn’t linear, and while the quarterback would like a few throws back, that’s how every quarterback feels at the end of the game. The young quarterback is looking more comfortable week to week, and while his mobility will never be elite, he looked a tad more limber today, and I expect that to continue as he gets further away from the knee injury. The offense can’t stall out during the middle of the fourth, but it is nice that the QB wasn’t the main reason for those negative series. Michael Penix Jr. throwing chart pic.twitter.com/F7nD7Hp3Kt — Tre’Shon (@tre3shon) October 25, 2026 The Falcons are now 3-4; their season is far from over, and the NFC South is still wide open . Atlanta needed to prove they could finish, and with this win under their belt, they proved they could do it. Enjoy the win!

stories.title: Burrow throws 4 TD passes as Bengals storm past Jackson-less Ravens in 2nd half of 35-13 win
stories.summary: — Joe Burrow threw four touchdown passes in the second half, and the Cincinnati Bengals rebounded from a desultory first two quarters to beat Baltimore 35-13 on Sunday, handing the Ravens a second straight divisional loss with Lamar Jackson sidelined.
stories.detailText: BALTIMORE -- — Joe Burrow threw four touchdown passes in the second half, and the Cincinnati Bengals rebounded from a desultory first two quarters to beat Baltimore 35-13 on Sunday, handing the Ravens a second straight divisional loss with Lamar Jackson sidelined. Baltimore (4-3) dominated the first half but led only 13-0 after settling for a couple of short field goals. Then the Ravens blew a double-digit second-half lead for the second straight week and 10th time since the start of the 2022 season. The Bengals (4-2) were shut out in their second meeting with Baltimore last season, and were scoreless through two quarters this time before going 66 yards on the first drive after halftime, capped by Burrow's 6-yard TD pass to Mike Gesicki . Baltimore, which held the ball for 22:20 in the first half, went three-and-out on its first possession of the second. Burrow's 13-yard scoring pass to Tee Higgins put Cincinnati ahead to stay. The Ravens put together one more decent drive, but on fourth-and-2 from the Cincinnati 12, Tyler Huntley threw incomplete. The Bengals then showed why Baltimore decided to be so aggressive, driving 88 yards and going up 21-13 on Samaje Perine 's 1-yard run. Burrow added a 2-yard scoring pass to Ja'Marr Chase and a 16-yarder to Drew Sample . Jackson missed a third straight game with an ankle injury, and the Ravens are 1-2 without him. He practiced in a limited role during the week but was inactive again. Baltimore's running game wasn't much of a factor without him, but Huntley threw for 215 yards in the first half — 120 of them to Zay Flowers . The shifty Flowers opened the scoring with a 48-yard catch-and-run. Cincinnati kept pouring it on after erasing the 13-0 deficit. Former Baltimore quarterback Joe Flacco relieved Burrow late, closing out the Ravens' fifth loss in their past six home games. Baltimore has outscored opponents by 65 points in the first half this season, while being outscored by 70 after the break. Injuries Bengals: S Kyle Dugger injured his quadriceps, and TE Erick All Jr . hurt his knee. Ravens: Rookie G Vega Ioane (knee) exited in the first half. Up next Bengals: Tennessee at home next Sunday. Ravens: At Buffalo next Sunday. ------ This story corrects a previous version with Cincinnati tight end Erick All Jr. injuring a knee, not cornerback DJ Turner II. ------ See AP’s full NFL coverage here

stories.title: Eye-catchers from Basha-Brophy Prep
stories.summary: Reigning Open Division state champions Chandler (Ariz.) Basha topped Phoenix (Ariz.) Brophy Prep, 42-17, in a key 6A regular season game...
stories.detailText: Reigning Open Division state champions Chandler (Ariz.) Basha topped Phoenix (Ariz.) Brophy Prep , 42-17, in a key 6A regular season game… ACC, Big Ten, Big 12 and SEC commits as well as Mountain West and Big Sky pledge were on the field as well as multiple Navy All-American’s and Polynesian Bowl selections. In addition, there were Rivals 300 members from the 2027 and 2028 classes plus three Rivals 150 members from the class of 2029 all playing. Here are our eye catchers from the game. Rivals Player of the Game: RB Noah Roberts, 2027 The Texas pledge ran for over 200 yards, with two touchdowns. One was a 40-yarder that set up the go-ahead touchdown right before the half and the second was right after the half, a 70-yarder where he cut it outside and went up the Basha sideline to paydirt. He looked much more like his sophomore season, with more burst and acceleration and didn’t try to break everything outside, working more on inside run and it paid off. More Eye Catchers Brophy Prep – Bishop Allen , CB, 2029 – The Rivals 150 member only had two tackles but was really good in coverage, showing physicality against the receiver he drew without allowing for much separation. – Ryder Noche , DB, 2027 – The Colgate commit did a little bit of everything for the Broncos, with eight tackles, a pass breakup and a blocked field goal and also had carries and receptions. He’s undersized but he’s a playmaker. – Noah Stewart , QB, 2028 – Against a pretty good defense, Stewart was under pressure for a chunk of the evening, but showed the willingness to stand in the pocket and had one of the best throws of the night with a hit bearing down on him, deliving a strike that set up their first touchdown of the night. He threw a touchdown later in the game to just one pick. – Mason Alexander , S, 2029 – The son of longtime NFL defensive lineman Lorenzo Alexander, the younger Alexander had four tackles, one for loss and a pass breakup. – Yuen Taufete’e , IOL, 2029 – In the early going when Brophy was making a threat, much of it was because of his blocking on the interior. The newcomer to the Rivals 150 is a pure guard and has the strength to drive his defender back while playing with a nasty streak. – Colin Itule , OT, 2029 – The Rivals 150 tackle held up against the relentless pressure of the loaded Basha defensive line, which featured four Division I lineman, and as he continues to get stronger, will be an even bigger force in college. He’s already very technically sound and has good footwork and hand placement. – Karter Chamblin , WR, 2030 – Chamblin had a team high five catches for 34 yards, but you could see the defense was geared toward limiting his downfield ability to impact the game. Basha – Anitoni Tahi , DL, 2028 – With Kansas State coaches looking on at the future Wildcat, in town to play, Tahi has an endless motor that gets a significant push to plug up holes in the running game. – TK Cunningham , EDGE, 2028 – The Purdue commit, who had Boilermaker coaches there watching him, is still pretty lean but he’s got a quick first step that gets him in to the backfield but he needs to just continue to develop a bigger arsenal of moves and continue to fill out for when he gets to the Big Ten. – Jaden Baldwin , WR, 2028 – Baldwin finished the game with eight receptions for 91 yards and a receiving touchdown while also running for a touchdown. The Pittsburgh commit is a legitimate downfield threat and routinely got himself open. – Caleb Jordan , EDGE, 2028 – Despite playing with a gigantic brace on his left arm, the Nevada commit showed no ill effects from it, and was able to get in to the backfield, when he wasn’t being held, and brought pressure consistently then showed his instincts breaking up a couple of passes. – Jake Rogers , QB, 2027 – The Princeton commit played with in himself, taking what the defense gave him and spreading the ball around instead of forcing passes and then was able to pick up some yards with his legs as well. – Jake Hildebrand , OT, 2027 – The No. 1 lineman in the state, committed to Arizona State , and had ASU offensive line coach Saga Tuitele there to watch him. Hildebrand has added a bunch of weight and strength in the offseason, and didn’t sacrifice any agility and looked every bit the best lineman in the state. – DaJohn Yarborough , IOL, 2027 – After a season-ending injury as a sophomore robbed him of the offseason, the Cal commit looks like he’s shed about 30 pounds since the summer and looks much closer to his junior self. He looked more agile and fresh in paving the way next to Hildebrand for Roberts. – Landen Wade , EDGE, 2028 – One of the premier prospects in the West in his class, the Rivals 100 edge Wade played more interior next to Cunningham, as a three-tech. He continues to look bigger and stronger but his quickness as a natural edge rusher gives him that initial burst off the line inside. – Marc Duerson , LB, 2028 – The Northern Arizona commit once again was all over the place for the Bears, seemingly in or around every tackle and despite the optimal linebacker size, he hits you like a traditional old-school linebacker. – Ahmad Jones , CB, 2030 – In the battle of top 2030’s, Jones may have gotten the upper hand on Chamblin in limiting his yards after catch, holding him to just five catches for 34 yards. It will be interesting to see what the 6-4 freshman’s body does the next few years, or if he can stay as a big corner, but his coverage ability is already attractive. – Jayden Tyus , CB, 2030 – Another 2030 who is playing significant snaps for the Bears, he’s not as big or long as Jones, but he’s plenty physical and showed no fear in coverage.

stories.title: Singletary's 30-yard run in OT gives Giants 27-21 win over Texans
stories.summary: — Devin Singletary’s 30-yard touchdown run in overtime lifted the New York Giants to a 27-21 win over the Houston Texans on Sunday.
stories.detailText: HOUSTON -- — Devin Singletary’s 30-yard touchdown run in overtime lifted the New York Giants to a 27-21 win over the Houston Texans on Sunday. Cam Skattebo had a 16-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter and his 42-yard scamper to set up Singletary’s game-winning run. He had 17 carries for 124 yards after not having a carry last Sunday following a costly fumble two weeks ago. J.J. McCarthy moved the ball effectively for the Giants (4-2-1) in his first start of the season after coach John Harbaugh benched Jameis Winston . He was 20 of 28 for 252 yards in the stadium in which he won the national title with Michigan in January 2024. The Texans (2-5) got the ball first in overtime, but New York’s defense forced a three-and-out with Kayvon Thibodeaux dropping a potential interception on second down. C.J. Stroud had two touchdown passes but finished with a season-low 153 yards passing as the Texans failed to move the ball for most of the second half. They tied it at 21-all on Xavier Hutchinson’s 3-yard grab with just under a minute to go. The Giants didn’t get into field-goal range before time ran out to send it to OT. The Giants took a 21-14 lead when Skattebo broke multiple tackles on a 16-yard touchdown run with about nine minutes remaining and celebrated with a backflip. Tank Dell had one reception for 43 yards and returned a punt for 14 yards in his return after missing almost two years recovering from a gruesome knee injury. The Texans had trouble moving the ball after halftime and punted on their first three possessions after the break before the touchdown by Hutchinson. Marvin Harrison Jr . scored a touchdown in the second quarter in his second game with the Texans after a trade with the Cardinals two weeks ago. The Texans were up 3-0 after an early field goal by Ka’imi Fairbairn when the Giants took the lead when Tyrone Tracy Jr . scored on a 2-yard run. That TD was set up by a 42-yard reception by Malik Nabers the play before. A 57-yard field goal by Fairbairn cut the lead to 7-6 with about nine minutes left in the second quarter. New York padded the lead when Winston plunged in from 1-yard out for a touchdown about 3 ½ minutes before halftime. McCarthy found Thomas Fidone II wide open for a 29-yard gain two plays earlier to put the Giants in scoring position. Stroud found Harrison in the back of the end zone on a 6-yard TD with about 30 seconds left in the second quarter. Cade Stover’s reception for the 2-point conversion tied it at 14-all. The Giants had a chance to take the lead after that but Dominic Zvada’s 44-yard field-goal attempt sailed wide right. It was his second miss of the game after his 56-yard attempt late in the first quarter was also wide right. Injuries Texans WR Jaylin Noel left in the fourth quarter with a toe injury. Up next Both teams are off next week before the Giants visit the Eagles on Nov. 8 and the Texans visit the Chargers that day. ------ See AP’s full NFL coverage here

stories.title: Giants beat Texans 27-21 in overtime
stories.summary: Giants RB Cam Skattebo ran 42 yards to the Houston 30 in OT, and Devin Singletary scored on next play.
stories.detailText: Cam Skattebo had no touches last week. He had 18 touches, 124 rushing yards, a touchdown and the longest run of his career set up the Giants for the overtime win. Skattebo went 42 yards to the Houston 30 on the Giants' second snap of overtime before former Texan Devin Singletary ran the rest of the way to the end zone on the next play. It handed the Giants a 27-21 victory with only 2:35 gone in OT. The Giants won in J.J. McCarthy's first start with the team and moved to 4-2-1, while the Texans' postseason hopes are likely gone with a 2-5 record. McCarthy's second career game-winning drive came after the Texans went three-and-out to start overtime. Giants edge rusher Kayvon Thibodeaux dropped an interception in his hands on the Texans' side of the 50 on the second play in overtime. The Texans tied the game with 52 seconds remaining in the fourth quarter when Xavier Hutchinson caught a 3-yard touchdown on third down. They didn't carry the momentum with them into overtime, though. The Giants had 34 carries for 188 yards and McCarthy went 20-for-28 for 252 yards. Malik Nabers caught seven passes for 111 yards. Singletary had five carries for 41 yards and the game-winning touchdown, and Tyrone Tracy six carries for 15 yards and a touchdown before a hamstring injury. Jameis Winston scored on a 1-yard quarterback sneak. The Giants outgained the Texans 420 to 237, but kicker Dominic Zvada missed field goals of 44 and 56 yards in the first half. C.J. Stroud was 17-of-28 for 153 yards and two touchdowns. Tank Dell, playing his first game since December 2024, caught a 43-yard pass and had a 14-yard punt return. Woody Marks had 19 carries for 66 yards. Ka'imi Fairbairn kicked first-half field goals of 57 and 58 yards.

stories.title: Deshaun Watson leads another game-winning drive as the Browns beat the Titans 27-24
stories.summary: — Deshaun Watson led his fifth game-winning drive in the fourth quarter this season, connecting with Harold Fannin Jr. on a 36-yard catch-and run that set up Andre Szmyt's 32-yard field goal...
stories.detailText: NASHVILLE, Tenn. -- — Deshaun Watson led his fifth game-winning drive in the fourth quarter this season, connecting with Harold Fannin Jr . on a 36-yard catch-and run that set up Andre Szmyt 's 32-yard field goal as time expired, and the Cleveland Browns beat the Tennessee Titans 27-24 on Sunday for their fifth win in six games. Watson ran for a touchdown and threw for 308 yards. Quinshon Judkins ran for 96 yards and two touchdowns, and rookie KC Concepcion caught eight passes for 129 yards in his best game yet. The AFC North-leading Browns (5-2) had two takeaways as they started a three-game road swing with a win. Szmyt got the chance with his game-winning kick to make up for clanking a 43-yarder off the right upright within the first minute of the fourth quarter. The Titans responded with a drive capped by a 29-yard field goal by Joey Slye , which tied the game at 17-all with 8:41 remaining. Watson responded with a 71-yard drive that he finished with a 9-yard TD run with 4:34 left. The Titans answered when Tony Pollard scored his career high-tying third TD with 58 seconds remaining. Slye’s extra point tied it at 24-all. Officials missed an apparent false start on the Browns when Watson found Fannin for the big gain. The Titans (1-6) came in trying to string together back-to-back wins for the first time in nearly four years. They had their best start to a game this season, taking a 14-0 lead with Pollard's two touchdowns. But Pollard was ruled down just outside the end zone in the second quarter, and Cleveland turned the Titans over on downs with Maliek Collins stopping Pollard on fourth-and-goal. Anthony Hill Jr . stripped Fannin of the ball after a catch, and safety Tony Adams recovered. Denzel Ward picked off Cam Ward on the next play. The Browns turned that takeaway into a 78-yard drive, capped by Judkins running for his second 5-yard TD. The Titans went three-and-out, giving Cleveland the ball back. Szmyt kicked a 28-yard field goal as time expired for a 17-14 halftime lead. Injuries Browns right tackle Tytus Howard was evaluated for a concussion after going down during Cleveland's opening drive of the third quarter. Cornerback Myles Harden hurt a hamstring but returned in the fourth quarter. Titans punter Tommy Townsend hurt a knee on a 44-yard punt late in the second quarter. Townsend stretched on the sideline, but placekicker Slye came out for a punt on fourth-and-1 only to be bailed out when Cleveland had 12 men on the field. Slye punted late in the third and had a 42-yarder on his first NFL punt. Up next The Browns visit Pittsburgh next Sunday. The Titans visit Cincinnati next Sunday. ------ See AP’s full NFL coverage here

stories.title: J.J. McCarthy, Cam Skattebo connect for Giants' 27-21 OT win against Texans
stories.summary: After several weeks of uncertainty in the Giants' QB and RB rooms, J.J. McCarthy and Cam Skattebo powered New York to 27-21 overtime win against the Houston Texans in Week 7.
stories.detailText: After several weeks of uncertainty in the Giants' QB and RB rooms, J.J. McCarthy and Cam Skattebo powered New York to a 27-21 overtime win against the Houston Texans in Week 7. The Giants improve to 4-2-1 with the win. Here are the takeaways... -- Though it took a few plays for the Giants' defense to warm up, the addition of Paulson Adebo and Tyler Nubin seemed to revitalize the secondary after a few very shorthanded weeks. Thanks to three solo tackles from Micah McFadden , New York held the Texans to a field goal in their opening drive. Ka'imi Fairbairn drove a 58-yard kick through the posts for the lead. The Giants responded quickly, easily grabbing a touchdown behind a fiery start from McCarthy. After opening his first drive as a starter with two tosses to Skattebo, Jamies Winston temporarily replaced McCarthy on the third offensive play of the game for a 3rd-and-short tush push before relinquishing the QB spot to McCarthy once again. He then crept up to 4th and 2 before launching a 42-yard pass toward Malik Nabers , who narrowly avoided Kamari Lassiter for the gain. Tyrone Tracy ran the ball into the end zone from the 2-yard line, and Dominic Zvada delivered the extra point for a 7-3 Giants edge. -- Two quick incompletions from C.J. Stroud lead to a Houston punt, giving the Giants possession once again. Despite another 40-plus yard toss from McCarthy — this time a 47-yarder to rookie wideout Malachi Fields down the sideline — two plays with negative yardage, a five-yard penalty, and an incomplete throw to Nabers forced the Giants into a 56-yard field goal attempt, which Zvada missed. McCarthy finished the first quarter 5-for-6 passing for 96 yards, averaging 16 yards per throw. -- The second frame began with a quick 3-and-out for each team. On their second drive, the Texans seemed to have figured out a way around the New York defense, but a false start by Ed Ingram on 4th-and-1 knocked them back five yards to New York's 39. Fairbairn's 57-yard field goal attempt was successful, closing the score gap to 7-6. McCarthy continued to shine as New York got the ball back, evading pressure by gliding through the pocket to buy time and keeping his eyes downfield for open receivers for an 11-yard pass to Nabers and a 29-yarder to Thomas Fidone , who landed just one yard shy of the end zone for his first NFL catch. Winston took the field once again for a sneak, and Zvada nailed the extra point kick for New York's second seven-point score. Earlier in the drive, Tracy strung together back-to-back runs worth 5 and 7 yards, respectively, before walking off the field slowly, seemingly nursing his leg. -- After holding the Texans to just 82 yards up to the two-minute warning, New York's defense started to lose its footing as the Texans marched 90 yards down the field in just seven plays to even the score. Houston first broke through with a 43-yard connection from Stroud to Tank Dell , who made his first catch in nearly two full seasons after rehabbing a gnarly knee injury he sustained Dec. 21, 2024. A 17-yard catch by Dalton Schultz put Houston on the 6, and a pinpoint TD pass to Marvin Harrison Jr. that flew past McFadden landed them in the end zone. A successful two-point conversion knotted the score at 14. With just 30 seconds left in the game, the Giants tried to regain their lead, but another missed field goal by Zvada — his fifth failed attempt in his last nine — ended the half. -- The third quarter was a slog for both teams. New York got the ball back to start the frame, but when McCarthy followed a six-yard run from Skattebo, a 20-yard pass to Fields, and a two-yard run from Devin Singletary with an interception and a five-yard sack at Houston's 32, the Giants elected to punt instead of going for the 55-yard field goal attempt given Zvada's kicking slump. Both teams then traded 3-and-outs. The momentum almost picked up on the Texans' second drive of the quarter, when McFadden recovered a Woody Marks fumble forced by Giants DL Bobby Jamison-Travis and ran 44 yards for the touchdown, but a replay revealed that Marks was not down by contact and the play was reversed. On his way down, Marks landed awkwardly on his knee and left the field as the referees determined the outcome of the play. Stroud then threw two more incompletions to end the drive, once again leaving the Giants 30 seconds of the quarter to work with. This time, New York took full advantage. A fake tush push allowed Skattebo to skirt a distracted Texans defense and rush 19 yards, the Giants' longest run of the day up to that point. A quick 4-yard toss to Darnell Mooney landed New York just outside Houston territory to end the frame. -- The Giants slowly chipped away yardage as the fourth quarter got underway, taking eight plays to move up to the Houston 30 before McCarthy dug the team out of a 3rd & 9 with a laser 14-yarder to Fields. He then handed the ball off to Skattebo, who dodged a flurry of Houston attacks and ran 16 yards to put the Giants up once again. Zvada's third successful extra point set the score at 21-14 with 8:55 to play. New York shut down Houston's next drive in Houston territory, but the Texans retaliated, notching their third sack of the day on an all-out blitz and forcing a punt from the Giants' 14. Starting inside the 50-yard line, the Texans strung together seven-straight gains before a 3-yard TD pass to Xavier Hutchinson and a good extra point attempt evened the score with less than a minute to go. Though they regained possession, the Giants were unable to move down the field quickly enough, sending the game to overtime for their second extra-time appearance of the season. -- The Texans opened overtime with the ball. Giants OL Kayvon Thibodeauz nearly ended Houston's run early with the first interception of the game but dropped the catch, resulting in another incomplete for Stroud. A second on the next toss meant Houston was forced to punt. After their lucky tie with the Washington Commanders in Week 5, the Giants were taking no chances this time around. After a nine-yard pass to Nabers to start the drive — bringing the wideout to 111 yards on the day for his fourth-straight 100-yard effort — Skattebo darted up the middle of the field nearly unchallenged for a 42-yard gain before running out of gas. A 30-yard touchdown run from Devin Singletary sealed the deal. -- Skattebo's team-leading 17 carries and 124 yards surely solidified his role as the team's starting running back once again, a hopeful start to his redemption arc after having his time severely cut in Week 6. Game MVP: J.J. McCarthy The 23-year-old quickly settled into his new role, completing 20 of his 28 passes for a total of 252 yards (99.1 percent pass rating). With his two long tosses in the first, he becomes the first Giants QB since Eli Manning in 2011 to complete two 40-plus-yard passes in his first game as the starter. stories.title: Browns move to 5-2 with another game-winning field goal, defeat Titans 27-24
stories.summary: Somehow, the Browns have done it again.
stories.detailText: Somehow, the Browns have done it again. With a 32-yard field goal as time expired, kicker Andre Szmyt gave Cleveland a 27-24 victory over Tennessee, keeping the club in a tie for first place in the AFC North. While the Titans had raced out to a 14-0 lead over the Browns — in part due to a Deshaun Watson interception — the Browns came back to take a 17-14 lead at halftime. Quinshon Judkins rushed for a pair of touchdowns and Szmyt hit a 28-yard field goal to go ahead. That score held until the fourth quarter, when Joey Slye hit a 29-yard field goal to tie it up. The Browns responded with a Watson rushing touchdown, going up 24-17 with 4:34 left in the contest. But the Titans tied it up again with Tony Pollard’s third rushing touchdown of the day. Once again, however, Watson was able to engineer a game-winning drive late in the fourth quarter. He hit tight end Harold Fannin over the middle for a catch-and-run, 36-yard gain — setting up Szmyt for a game-winning field goal. Though Szmyt banged a 43-yard attempt off the right upright earlier in the fourth quarter, his 32-yard, game-winning attempt was true as time expired. Watson played one of his best games in a Browns uniform, as the offense put up a season-high 491 yards. Cleveland’s previous high was 372 in the Week 4 win over Pittsburgh. The quarterback finished 25-of-36 for 308 yards with an interception. It's the first time Watson has thrown for 300 yards with the Browns. He also had three carries for 19 yards with a touchdown. Watson has now led a fourth-quarter or overtime game-winning drive in all four of the Browns’ wins. The last time a Browns quarterback had at least five game-winning drives was Bernie Kosar in 1986. KC Concepcion had eight catches for 129 yards, setting a new career high. He also had three carries for 23 yards. Quinshon Judkins had his best game of the season, rushing for 96 yards with two TDs while also catching an 8-yard pass. On the other side, Cam Ward was 20-of-31 for 181 yards with an interception. Pollard, who rushed for a career-high 161 when the Titans played the Browns last year, had 129 yards on 25 carries with three touchdowns. He also had three catches for 26 yards. Titans punter Tommy Townsend suffered a knee injury and was unable to punt during the second half, with Joey Slye taking over the duties. Townsend stayed in the game to serve as a holder. Now at 5-2, the Browns will be on the road again to face Pittsburgh with first place in the division on the line next week. The 1-6 Titans will be on the road to play the Bengals.

stories.detailText: HOUSTON, TEXAS - OCTOBER 25: Cade Stover #8 of the Houston Texans celebrates a two point conversion with Ed Ingram #69 of the Houston Texans during the second quarter against the New York Giants at NRG Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Kenneth Richmond/Getty Images) | Getty Images We are seven games into the season and we are still stuck with the central question when it comes to the Houston Texans: what exactly are you? Are they a passing team that gives up fourteen penalties a game (like they did today, of which 10 were accepted)? Are they a smashmouth team with a defense that can stop anybody (except in overtime when they got absolutely steamrolled by Cam Skattebo and the Giants)? Are they good? Are they bad? Well, today’s 27-21 loss to the New York Giants, those last two questions feel pretty irrelevant. They are what they are and boy are they ever that. Texans played down to their opponents yet again, racking up 237 yards of total offense a touchdown pass to Marvin Harrison Jr. (his first with the Texans) and an Xavier Hutchinson rush are the only touchdowns the Texans could get. And the defense simply had no answers for J.J. McCarthy and Cam Skattebo. I want you to read that statement again. The Houston Texans defense had no answers for a pretty pedestrian Giants offense; which they allowed to score 27 points and 420 yards of total offense. But most of all, we need to talk about Kamari Lassiter. Something is clearly wrong and his play has suffered as a result. Also, too, the defense is weak against explosive plays now. That’s fun. At any rate, this week is over, possibly the season, and the Texans go into their off week with way more questions in front of them than a Super Bowl caliber team should encounter at this point of the season.

stories.title: Falcons' Kendal Daniels, a week after scary neck injury, recovers fumble late to help lift Atlanta past San Francisco
stories.summary: Kendal Daniels was carted off the field last week after a scary neck injury he suffered against the Chicago Bears.
stories.detailText: Kendal Daniels appears to be perfectly fine. Daniels, a week removed from a scary neck injury that forced him to be stretchered off the field , came up with a game-sealing fumble recovery Sunday afternoon to lift the Atlanta Falcons past the San Francisco 49ers . The Falcons were up nine late at Mercedes-Benz Stadium, trying to fend off one last-ditch effort from the 49ers. With less than a minute left, San Francisco tight end George Kittle caught a wide open pass and was breaking to the middle of the field, seemingly putting the 49ers into scoring position. But Jessie Bates III dove for Kittle's legs and managed to trip him up. As he was stumbling forward, Kittle lost the ball, allowing Daniels to fly in and land on it untouched. The rookie Kendal Daniels makes the play again! @AtlantaFalcons force the fumble and recover it to seal the win over San Francisco pic.twitter.com/9o2xsWnT2e — NFL (@NFL) October 25, 2026 That secured the 29-20 win for the Falcons, and handed the 49ers their first loss of the season. Daniels ended up leading the Falcons with a career-high 11 total tackles Sunday, nine of which he did by himself. While the fumble recovery was the most important, he was a force for Atlanta’s defense all afternoon. He even intercepted Brock Purdy late in the fourth quarter, which was one of four turnovers the Falcons forced Sunday. Daniels, whom the Falcons took in the fourth round of the NFL Draft out of Oklahoma, is up to 40 total tackles this season. Sunday's outing came on the heels of a scary injury in their Week 7 matchup with the Chicago Bears. Daniels came flying in to try and tackle Bears tight end Colston Loveland, and he remained down on the field for roughly 10 minutes before being carted off. Kendal Daniels Is Currently Being Stretched Off The Field. Praying He’s OK. Scary. 😬 pic.twitter.com/h26LcWj0Sz — SM Highlights (@SMHighlights1) October 18, 2026 Days later, Daniels was back at practice and was cleared to return. "I scared a lot of people," Daniels said, via the Atlanta Journal-Constitution . "It was a scary play. I'm blessed to come out how I did, and it was a bang-bang play, but I'm happy I'm here." The Falcons (3-4) will take on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers (2-5) next week in Florida. And Daniels, now with his terrifying neck injury behind him, can keep pushing forward in what has been an already impressive rookie campaign.

stories.title: Malik Willis sparks Dolphins' first win, holding off a late Jets rally 28-25
stories.summary: — Malik Willis threw two touchdown passes and ran for a score, leading the Miami Dolphins to their first win of the season with a 28-25 victory over the New York Jets on Sunday.
stories.detailText: EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- — Malik Willis threw two touchdown passes and ran for a score, leading the Miami Dolphins to their first win of the season with a 28-25 victory over the New York Jets on Sunday. The Dolphins (1-5) came off their bye-week break and avoided their first 0-6 start since 2019 by scoring on their first two drives and controlling most of the game before holding on to give coach Jeff Hafley his first win. Trailing 28-17 with 4:44 left, the Jets (2-5) made a late push. On fourth-and-4, Geno Smith completed a short pass to Isaiah Davis , who zipped downfield 41 yards to the Dolphins 18. Three plays later, Smith found Mason Taylor in the back left corner of the end zone for a 12-yard touchdown, the tight end's second of the game. Penalties negated New York's first two 2-point tries before Smith threw to Taylor to make it 28-25 with 3:24 left. But Willis sealed the victory when he pushed forward for 2 yards on fourth-and-1 as the Dolphins celebrated and frustrated Jets fans filed out of MetLife Stadium. Willis was 14 of 21 for 208 yards and two TD passes to rookie Caleb Douglas , and ran for 37 yards on eight carries. Ollie Gordon rushed for 103 yards and a score. Smith was 23 of 30 for 287 yards and three touchdowns, the two to Taylor and another to Omar Cooper Jr ., and an interception. Braelon Allen had 104 yards rushing for the Jets, who dropped to 0-8 against AFC East opponents under Aaron Glenn. Dolphins and Jets start things off with a scoring spree The Dolphins started quickly, marching 76 yards on seven plays and taking their first lead in any game this season on Willis' 7-yard touchdown pass to Douglas. It also ended New York's streak of not allowing any points on an opening possession in five straight games. But the Jets came right back as Smith connected with Cooper for a 52-yard gain on their first offensive snap. Three plays later, Taylor — son of former Dolphins star and Pro Football Hall of Famer Jason Taylor — reached over Jason Marshall Jr . in the back of the end zone for a 13-yard score that tied it at 7. It's the third straight game in which New York scored on its opening drive. Miami then went on a 14-play, 60-yard run that was capped by Gordon's 1-yard touchdown run. New York was driving again on its next possession at the Miami 21 when Smith tried to fit a pass through a tight window to Taylor, but Michael Taaffe stepped in front and intercepted it. The Dolphins' touchdown streak ended on their third possession, though, when they went three-and-out. They got right back at it on their next drive, with Willis scoring on a 2-yard scramble with 6 seconds left in the first half to take a 21-7 lead. Jets' woes extend into the second half Allen gave New York some immediate second-half juice with a 27-yard run on the Jets' first play of the third quarter, but the drive stalled. Adding to the misery, Jason Sanders — a longtime Dolphins kicker in his first season with the Jets — hit the right upright on a 40-yard try. Cooper got New York's next drive started with a 60-yard reception, and ended it five plays later with a 3-yard touchdown catch to make it a one-score game at 21-14 with 5:50 left in the third quarter. The Jets later got to the Dolphins 1, but couldn't punch it in on runs by Andrew Beck and Allen and settled for a 33-yard field goal when Smith was sacked on third down. Willis side-armed a short toss to Douglas, who tiptoed the sideline after the catch and raced down the sideline for a 63-yard touchdown that put Miami up 28-17 with 4:44 remaining. Injuries Dolphins: S Dante Trader Jr . injured his left shoulder in the third quarter. ... CB JuJu Brents left with a stinger in the second half, but returned in the fourth quarter. Jets: DT T'Vondre Sweat limped off with a knee injury late in the second quarter and didn't return. Up next Dolphins: Host New England next Sunday. Jets: Host Las Vegas next Sunday. ------ See AP’s full NFL coverage here

stories.title: Browns 27 Titans 24 quick recap

stories.detailText: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - OCTOBER 25: Tony Pollard #20 of the Tennessee Titans avoids a tackle from Denzel Ward #21 of the Cleveland Browns during the first quarter at Nissan Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images Well, at least that was an exciting loss, I guess. The Tennessee Titans will have to wait at least another three weeks to win their first back-to-back wins since 2022 (they have their bye after next week). The Titans got off to a fast start in this one. Tony Pollard ran all over the Browns in the first quarter with two rushing touchdowns on the first two possessions. The second was set up by a Cor’Dale Flott interception of Deshaun Watson. Unfortunately, the Titans wouldn’t score again until Joey Slye kicked a 29-yard field goal with 8:41 left in the fourth quarter. That’s the product of the offense continuing to be inconsistent. That field goal tied the game at 17. After the Browns scored a touchdown to go up 24-17, Cam Ward and the Titans put together an 11-play, 63-yard touchdown drive that ended with Pollard scoring his third touchdown of the day from 1 yard out. The hope was that the game would get to overtime. It did not. The Browns went 55 yards in just 4 plays to set up the game-winning field goal. There was plenty of good in this game. The Titans have a stud in Carnell Tate. He had 5 catches for 69 yards, including a really nice 18-yard catch to set up Pollard’s game-tying touchdown. Now, they just need to find a quarterback who can play consistently enough to sustain an offense for 4 quarters.

stories.title: Michael Penix Jr. throws 3 TD passes, Falcons force 4 turnovers to give 49ers first loss, 29-20
stories.summary: — Michael Penix Jr. threw three touchdown passes, Atlanta scored 13 points off four turnovers and the Falcons handed the San Francisco 49ers their first loss, 29-20 on Sunday.
stories.detailText: ATLANTA -- — Michael Penix Jr . threw three touchdown passes, Atlanta scored 13 points off four turnovers and the Falcons handed the San Francisco 49ers their first loss, 29-20 on Sunday. San Francisco (6-1) was already thin at wide receiver before its offense faced additional limitations when running back Christian McCaffrey missed much of the first half with a thigh injury. Rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels intercepted Brock Purdy 's pass intended for Jordan Watkins with 2:34 remaining. It was Purdy's second interception. Daniels then recovered a fumble by George Kittle with less than a minute remaining. The 49ers had only six turnovers in their first six games. Penix threw scoring passes to tight ends Nick Muse and Kyle Pitts before giving Atlanta (3-4) a 26-14 lead with a 21-yard touchdown pass to Drake London in the fourth quarter. Penix completed 25 of 34 passes for 213 yards with no interceptions. The 49ers' comeback attempt was hurt when a lengthy review by the officials took away Purdy's apparent 23-yard touchdown pass to Watkins. Following the ruling, Purdy was sacked on fourth down by Za'Darius Smith . Purdy's 1-yard scoring pass to fullback Kyle Juszcyk with 5:05 remaining cut Atlanta's lead to 26-20 before Eddy Pineiro extra-point attempt was wide left — his fourth miss of the season. A shanked punt by Atlanta's Jake Bailey allowed San Francisco to start a possession at its 47 with about four minutes remaining. The 49ers wasted the excellent field position and opportunity to mount a go-ahead drive when Purdy threw his second interception that led to Nick Folk 's 31-yard field goal. Purdy completed 27 of 40 passes for 288 yards with one touchdown and the two picks. Bijan Robinson rushed for 63 yards as the Falcons snapped a two-game skid. McCaffrey was limited to seven carries for 39 yards. McCaffrey's backup, Kaelon Black , lost a fumble at the Atlanta 29 that was recovered by Gervon Dexter Sr . in the second quarter. A long Atlanta drive set up Nick Folk's 33-yard field goal. In the third quarter, Jessie Bates III intercepted Purdy's pass at the Atlanta 10 to set up the touchdown drive capped by the scoring pass to London. The 49ers leaned heavily on McCaffrey on their opening touchdown drive. McCaffrey had two catches for 40 yards, including a 24-yard gain to the Atlanta 5. He had four carries for 29 yards, including a scoring fourth-down leap over the pile from the 1. McCaffrey had a 5-yard catch on the 49ers' next drive before leaving the game with the thigh injury. He was listed as questionable to return as he was examined in the injury tent. McCaffrey emerged, put on his helmet and tested the thigh by running on the sideline before heading to the locker room. Black's 30-yard scoring run on the first play of the second quarter gave San Francisco a 14-3 lead. McCaffrey returned for the second half and was used as a decoy on some plays. Injuries 49ers: Depth was an issue at wide receiver with starters Mike Evans (Achilles tendinitis) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring) inactive. Safety Marques Sigle (ankle) also was inactive. Falcons: Cornerback A.J. Terrell (groin) started after coming off injured reserve but his brother, rookie cornerback Avieon Terrell (back), was inactive. Up next 49ers: Following a bye week, host Las Vegas on Nov. 8. Falcons: Visit Tampa Bay next Sunday. ------ See AP’s full NFL coverage here

stories.title: Cleveland Browns rookie WR hits historic mark against Titans
stories.summary: KC Concepcion’s 129 receiving yards places him in the Top 10 for a single game by a rookie in franchise history.
stories.detailText: (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns have had several notable wide receivers in franchise history. Dante Lavelli and Mac Speedie in the 1940s and 1950s. Gary Collins and Paul Warfield in the 1960s. Reggie Rucker and Dave Logan in the 1970s. Webster Slaughter, Brian Brennan, and Reggie Langhorne in the 1980s. But very few had a day during their rookie seasons like the one KC Concepcion had on Sunday against the Tennessee Titans. Concepcion lit up the Titans for 129 receiving yards, a total that puts him at No. 8 on the franchise’s all-time list for receiving yards by a rookie wide receiver in a single game. Derrick Alexander holds the franchise record of 171 yards, set in 1994 in a game against the New York Giants. Concepcion looked to be on track to top Alexander, but just missed a deep pass in the third quarter and was shut out in the entire second half. He still contributed, however, as a key run in the fourth quarter set up a Deshaun Watson touchdown. Unlike Concepcion, Alexander’s record day came in a Week 13 loss as the Browns committed five turnovers and committed 11 penalties. Alexander finished with seven receptions, including a 60-yarder with about five minutes remaining that set up a game-tying touchdown. That was actually one of two big days that season for Alexander, as he had a 136-yard game against the Arizona Cardinals in a Week 3 victory. The new Top 10 for most receiving yards by a Browns rookie, according to statemuse.com , is now: Derrick Alexander, 171 yards in 1994 Mohamed Massaquoi, 148 yards in 2009 Derrick Alexander, 136 yards in 1994 Kevin Johnson, 135 yards in 1999 Webster Slaughter, 134 yards in 1986 Greg Little, 131 yards in 2011 Kevin Johnson, 131 yards in 1999 KC Concepcion, 129 yards in 2026 Paul Warfield, 126 yards in 1964 Paul Warfield 123 yards in 1964 Concepcion now has 30 catches for 315 yards on the season. stories.title: Jets hand Dolphins their first win of 2026 with 28-25 loss
stories.summary: The New York Jets lost, 28-25, Sunday at home against the AFC East rival Miami Dolphins
stories.detailText: If any Jets fans were hoping for an easy win against the 0-5 Miami Dolphins, they were in for a rude awakening. Miami stormed to a 21-7 first half lead and led the rest of the way. They held on to hand the Jets a devastating 28-25 loss and drop them to 2-5 on the season. The game got off to a terrible start for the Jets, as Miami drove the length of the field to open the scoring on Malik Willis ’ touchdown pass to rookie wideout Caleb Douglas . New York responded well, as Geno Smith connected with Omar Cooper on a 53-yard pass and then found Mason Taylor with a red zone touchdown pass. However, Miami again drove downfield and scored another touchdown, this time on Ollie Gordon II ’s one-yard run to take a 14-7 first quarter lead. The Jets offense struggled to get anything going for the rest of the half, with Smith throwing an interception for the second game in a row. The Dolphins were able to capitalize and take a 21-7 half-time lead on Willis’ touchdown scramble with six seconds left in the half. Things went from bad to worse for the Jets on their next possession, as the drive stalled in Miami territory and Jason Sanders hit the upright on a 40-yard field goal attempt. However, they got the ball back and Smith again connected on a big play to Cooper, this time for 60 yards. This time, Cooper finished off the drive himself on a three-yard pass from Smith to cut it to 21-14. New York drove down to Miami’s one-yard line in the fourth quarter with a chance to tie the score but had to settle for a Sanders field goal after three plays in a row lost yardage. Having struggled to get anything going on offense in the second half, Miami made it a two-possession game again when Willis hit Douglas and it ended up being a 63-yard touchdown as Minkah Fitzpatrick missed the tackle. That made it 28-17 with 4:44 remaining. The Jets hit back quickly, with Smith connecting on a touchdown pass to Taylor for the second time. They also connected on the two-point conversion to make it 28-25 with 3:24 remaining. However, Miami was able to run out the clock to secure their first win of the season. Here are the takeaways... -- The Jets seemed to learn nothing from the loss to the Patriots, as all of the issues that let them down in that game were problematic again. They didn’t execute well on third and fourth down on either side of the ball, once again gave up a score in the last two minutes of the first half, and struggled to get Garrett Wilson involved on offense and had issues in the red zone. -- Cooper had another huge game after his rookie of the week performance last week, but the Jets struggled to get any of their other weapons going in the passing game. Wilson, Kenyon Sadiq and the returning Adonai Mitchell combined for just three catches for 32 yards. Wilson was desperately imploring with Smith to get him the ball midway through the fourth quarter . -- Braelon Allen got off to a slow start, but once again ended up having a big performance with over 100 rushing yards and some good contributions in the passing game. Breece Hall was almost healthy enough to return for this game, but it’s difficult to know whether he would have made much of a difference -- New York’s defense struggled to get off the field for most of the first three quarters before starting to tighten up in the fourth quarter. However, they clearly aren’t a good enough offensive team to spot opposing teams a double-digit lead every week and expect to be able to get back in the game. -- The Jets lost nose tackle T’Vondre Sweat to a knee injury in the fourth quarter and that cost them, as Miami had some success running the ball at key moments in the second half as Gordon ended up with over 100 rushing yards. -- With Jarvis Brownlee inactive, rookie D’Angelo Ponds had to play a bigger role than he has in any game so far this season. He held his own for the most part, making one nice play in coverage and a couple of good tackles. However, his costly penalty in the end zone set up one of Miami’s first half touchdowns. Game MVP: Dolphins QB Malik Willis Willis was the driving force behind Miami’s strong first half, as he threw a touchdown pass and ran for another. He also crucially kept drives alive by rushing for five first downs, including on fourth down to ice the win. He only had 15 second half passing yards with five minutes to go but then delivered the decisive blow with his second touchdown pass to Douglas to end up with 208 yards and two touchdowns.
