Moton left the 43-13 loss to the Buccaneers with a leg injury and head coach Dave Canales told reporters at a postgame press conference that Moton has suffered a fractured fibula. Moton will miss a significant amount of time as a result. There's no good time for an injury like that, but the timing is particularly rough for Moton as he just returned from missing the first four games of the season while recovering from blood clots in his lungs. First-round pick Monroe Freeling replaced Moton during that absence and he'll likely be back in the lineup as long as he's healthy enough to play.

stories.title: Falcons – 49ers instant recap: A delightful upset against an undefeated team
stories.summary: The Falcons knock off the undefeated 49ers in Atlanta in a tremendous game.
stories.detailText: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 25: Drake London #5 of the Atlanta Falcons celebrates with teammates Austin Hooper #81 and Chris Blair #19 after scoring a touchdown against the San Francisco 49ers during the fourth quarter at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images An undefeated 49ers team coming to town, where the Falcons had yet to win, seemed like a recipe for disaster. Even with the 49ers mightily banged up, they had gone 6-0 to this point and the Falcons had been struggling. It was not always pretty and it certainly wasn’t easy, but these Falcons showed an incredible amount of talent, heart, and savvy in this one to come away with a 29-20 win. The defense forced four turnovers, the offense put together some impressive drives, special teams finally gave Atlanta favorable field position, and Atlanta got their first home win of the 2026 season against a formerly undefeated team. It was a glorious, messy win that once again reminded us of what this team can be, and a sorely needed one after two tough losses in a row. Who knows what this team can be when all is said and done, but the tenacity and will on Sunday was a thing of beauty and hopefully is a sign of better days to come. With the Panthers getting smoked by the Buccaneers, Atlanta is right back in the division and has all the opportunity in the world in front of them. What a day. Here’s a drive-by-drive recap of the game you just watched. 1st Quarter Atlanta kicked it off to open things up, and the 49ers got a seam and took it across the 35 yard line. The 49ers opened up their drive with a jump offsides by Trent Williams. Christian McCaffrey evaded defenders and picked up five yards before Xavier Watts got him. McCaffrey then plunged up the middle, with the Falcons reacting late to the delayed handoff and allowing him to run for almost a first down. McCaffrey then slinked through the middle of the line and picked 14 yards. A quick pass to McCaffrey over the middle got 16 yards and another first down. Kendal Daniels then got Kaelon Black for a small loss. Purdy then hung in with pressure lagging and found McCaffrey again for 24 yards. Black then got the handoff and got four yards, with Atlanta dropping him just shy of a touchdown. Black was then stopped cold by LaCale London as he ran up the middle. On his third straight carry, the Falcons stopped Black again. McCaffrey then leaped over the top of the defense and got far enough to score the touchdown on fourth down. 7-0 49ers. Zachariah Branch finally broke one, getting a lane and running 61 yards on the kickoff return. Bijan Robinson took it 11 on first down, and followed that up with seven more yards. Michael Penix Jr. then tried to hit Branch on second down, but didn’t connect. On 3rd and 3, Bijan got tackled for a three yard loss by Fred Warner. Nick Folk hit the 39 yard field goal try to make it 7-3 49ers. The 49ers got it past the 30. McCaffrey made a fully extended sideline grab for five yards. Black then took it for a yard before London got him. Purdy then hit George Kittle for a first down. An all-out rush on first down then took down Purdy, as Maason Smith got home for a sack. Smith then deflected the Purdy pass. A quick swing pass to the fullback was stopped by Harold Perkins Jr., setting up a punt. Jahan Dotson made the fair catch at about the 10. Bijan took the opening handoff for three yards. A quick swing pass to Robinson went nowhere with a defender right in his face, and he lost three yards. A 12 men in the huddle penalty backed the Falcons up. Penix then hit Austin Hooper for nine yards. Punt, and the 49ers caught it around the 38 yard line. 2nd Quarter Purdy rolled out and got Kittle for a first down. Black ran for a first down, and the 49ers declined a neutral zone infraction on Jared Ivey. Black then rolled for about seven yards before Daniels got him. Then Black got loose and ran for a 30 yard touchdown to put the 49ers up 14-3. Penix scrambled for two yards and then hit Bijan for a 15 yard pickup and a first down. Bijan took it six yards, and then Bijan was stymied for a gain of a yard. Penix then hit Drake London for a first down. Penix then found Charlie Woerner for nine yards, with Woerner spinning through contact. Bijan then fought through contact for another first down. A flip to Bijan was then flipped to Branch on the reverse, who ran for eight yards to the sideline. A swing pass to Khalil Herbert picked up 19 yards and almost went for a score, with Chris Blair with a tremendous box out block. The Falcons challenged the spot but didn’t win the challenge. Penix then hit a wide open Nick Muse for a touchdown. 14-9 49ers after Nick Folk doinked the extra point try. The 49ers got to the 30 on their return. Purdy tried for Brandin Cooks, his first throw to a receiver, and missed. Black then pushed his way through the pile for seven yards. Purdy then hit on the sideline for a first down. A toss to Black was stopped after maybe a yard. An end-around to Jacob Cowing went for ten yards. Purdy under pressure was able to flip it to Jordan James, who got 11 yards and a first down. James then took another carry and pushed his way forward for close to eight yards, but fumbled with an assist from Xavier Watts; the 49ers got it back. On the next carry, Black ran into the defense and fumbled with an assist from Maason Smith, with Gervon Dexter recovering. Penix hit London on first down for seven yards. A faked handoff to Robinson gave way to a pass under pressure to Kyle Pitts, who got two yards. A direct snap to Woerner went for a first down (really). Bijan then rolled ahead for five yards. Bijan then plunged ahead for a first down. Penix under pressure found Muse for a yard. Penix then hit Pitts for six yards. Penix then tried to get Jahan Dotson crossing over the middle, but Dotson just didn’t catch it. The Falcons got the 49ers to jump offsides on fourth down, somehow. Penix then got Branch, who dove forward for a first down. Penix then got a first down throw to Dotson. Then Penix hit Bijan on the sideline, who just got out of bounds with seven seconds yet. Penix then threw it out of bounds in the direction of London with two seconds left. Folk then hit the 33 yard field goal try to make it 14-12 49ers. 3rd Quarter Khalil Herbert dropped the kickoff but didn’t let it slow him, rolling past the 40 yard line on the kickoff return. A quick flip to Pitts got the Falcons started with nine yards. Bijan plunged ahead for about five yards. Then Penix hit Hooper for 11 yards and a first down, with Hooper getting in a nice stiff arm. Robinson took a delayed handoff for a yard. Pitts then reeled in a short screen pass as Penix was pressured, picking up three yards. Penix then found London over the middle, who stayed on his feet forever because he’s Drake London. Herbert then took the handoff for a couple of yards. London then caught another one over the middle and plunged forward to the five yard line. On the next play, Penix calmly rolled out and hit Kyle Pitts for a touchdown, Pitts’ fourth scoring grab in the past three weeks. 19-14 Falcons. Jordan James got past the 30 before DeMarcco Hellams got him. A diving Jordan Watkins got the 15 yard first down grab. xDexter then took down McCaffrey for a loss. Kittle then caught a first down. Purdy had forever on a rollout and hit a tight end for a first down. A swing pass to Black went for a four yard loss after Perkins got him. Then Purdy threw an interception on what was intended to be a throwaway to Jessie Bates. A slant to London went for eight yards, and London exited for a check after a 49ers defender went helmet-to-helmet with him. Bijan then took it three yards for a first down. Robinson then rolled for over 25 yards, but a holding call on Atlanta backed it up. Penix then skipped one to the sideline looking for Chris Blair. Penix then hauled one back downfield for Dotson, looking for a deep completion, but missed…only it didn’t matter because there were two fouls on the play, including an illegal contact the Falcons accepted to earn a free first down. Bijan then rolled for about six yards, and followed that up with a maximum effort one yard run. A quick pass to Bijan on the sideline went for 19 yards. Bijan then took it two yards on first down. Under pressure, Penix threw the ball away. Penix under pressure again then chucked it toward Dotson, but another pass interference call gave the Falcons a big gain and a first down. Herbert then took it eight yards. Penix then tried an open London but missed high. Bijan plunged ahead for the first down, and two calls on the defense again helped the Falcons further, with an offsides call on the 49ers giving more yardage. Then Penix threw a beauty to London, who dove for a touchdown. 26-14 Falcons. 4th Quarter Black picked up three yards on first down. Purdy then fired one deep to Watkins for 35 yards. A good gain was backed up by a holding call. A fullback pass got 11 yards. Then Purdy got Watkins again for a first down and more…but it was ultimately ruled incomplete. Purdy then threw it a little bit behind Cooks and it went incomplete. Purdy then got Jacob Cowing for 11 yards and a first down. Purdy then fired one deep into the end zone for Watkins, who caught it for a touchdown….until the review said he didn’t have possession coming down. On the next play, Purdy missed Black high. Purdy then threw it toward McCaffrey, but low and early. On fourth down, Za’Darius Smith got Purdy for a sack to end the drive. Ryan Neuzil snapped the ball over Penix’s head on first down. A quick swing pass to Robinson went for six yards. A quick pass to London was then latereled to Bijan for very close to a first down and 16 yards. The Falcons then tried to draw the 49ers offsides and failed, setting up a punt. It was fair caught at the 18 yard line. Purdy hit Cowing for a first down and 18 yards. Purdy tried to hit Kittle but it fell incomplete. McCaffrey took it up the gut for nine yards. Purdy then snuck it up the middle for a first down. Purdy then took a deep shot downfield, but it fell incomplete; a defensive holding call gave the 49ers five yards and a first down. Purdy then hit McCaffrey for five yards working against Perkins. Under pressure, Purdy kept moving and found Watkins for a first down, and then a facemask on Za’Darius Smith gave the 49ers more yards. Purdy then got Kittle for 11 yards and a first down. A fake handoff and quick toss to Kittle got four yards. Purdy then got McCaffrey again, just shy of a touchdown. Then Purdy got Kyle Jusczyk for a touchdown, but the 49ers missed the extra point. 26-20 Falcons. Bijan was swallowed up on first down, losing three yards. Penix then threw a quick out to London, who couldn’t come up with it. On third down, Dotson appeared to stop his route looking for a ball sooner, and then Penix threw it a mile and it fell incomplete. Punt, and it was shanked by Jake Bailey. One yard for the 49ers on first down. Purdy then hit McCaffrey for five yards. The 49ers were then hit with an offsides, and then Kendal Daniels made the play of the game, reaching up and knocking a Purdy pass off course and then intercepting it and returning it a long way down the field. Bijan took it three yards on first down, and then another two yards on second down. Bijan then took it another yard and the clock wound down to the two minute warning. Nick Folk then hit the 31 yard field goal to make it 29-20 Falcons. After the 49ers got it to about the 30 yard line, he hit Cowing for seven yards. Mike Hughes then broke up the pass intended for Kittle. Purdy then snucked forward to pick up the first down. Purdy then hit Cooks for a first down, with the clock still running. Purdy then spiked it. On the next play, Kittle got a big gain, but Bates punched it loose and Daniels fell on it. The Falcons kneeled it out.

stories.title: NFL Week 7 Winners and Losers: 49ers undefeated no more, as injuries finally too much to overcome in loss to Falcons
stories.summary: The 49ers finally lost after a 6-0 start to the season.
stories.detailText: The San Francisco 49ers' injuries finally caught up to them. The 49ers battled the Atlanta Falcons, which was commendable given their long injury report. But trailing 26-20 late, Brock Purdy threw an interception to linebacker Kendal Daniels. That was it for the 49ers and their undefeated streak to start the season. They are 6-1 after the Falcons won 29-20 . Losing a road game that was an early start in the Eastern Time Zone isn't a big deal for a team that was 6-0 and up multiple games in the division. Nobody expected the 49ers to go 17-0. The problem isn't a single loss. It's the injuries. Most other teams dealing with the 49ers' list of injuries would be closer to winless than undefeated. They overcame numerous injuries last season to make the playoffs and then were dealt the same hand this season. Last season and through six games this season, 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan found a way to get his team to rise above it. Sunday brought a new challenge, and that was playing without wide receivers. San Francisco had six receivers either inactive or on injured reserve. Mike Evans is dealing with an Achilles injury and left the team's Week 6 game early due to it. In Week 7 Evans was inactive. That meant Brandin Cooks, who is 33 and hasn't posted a 1,000-yard season since 2021, and Jordan Watkins, who had five career catches before Sunday, started at receiver against the Falcons. It wasn't just receiver injuries. Defensive end Nick Bosa missed another game. Christian McCaffrey had to manage a thigh injury during the game. If it was a normal team, even injuries wouldn't be a big deal. Players like Evans and Bosa should be back soon. Every team deals with it. But the 49ers have been the most injured team in the NFL over the past few seasons, and while that seems like terrible luck, it's not turning around. It's also an older team, especially among the elite stars, so more injuries and wearing down over a long season are concerns. And there's a dropoff to their second team. Without Evans, Deebo Samuel Sr. and other receivers the 49ers got very little out of their wideouts. With McCaffrey banged up, rookie Kaelon Black fumbled on back-to-back plays, losing the second one. That lost fumble changed the game's momentum. The 49ers are off to a great start and one loss doesn't change that. They're still in good shape in the NFC West. But it was the first time the 49ers couldn't overcome their injuries. And now they have to hope that, somehow, the bad injury luck doesn't continue. Here are the rest of the winners and losers from Week 7 of the NFL season: WINNERS J.J. McCarthy and Cam Skattebo: They each dealt with adversity this season. McCarthy was traded by the Minnesota Vikings and Skattebo found himself deep in the doghouse a week ago. They both teamed up for an impressive 27-21 upset win over the Houston Texans in overtime on Sunday . McCarthy got the start after a hot finish to last week's loss as Jameis Winston's replacement. It was a tough assignment on the road against a good Texans defense, but McCarthy played well. He went 20-of-28 passing for 252 yards. Skattebo shined too after being practically benched last week. He got no carries against the Saints in Week 6 after fumbling in overtime the week before, but on Sunday he came up with a huge play, a 42-yard run in overtime that got the Giants in field-goal range. They didn't need the field goal as Devin Singletary walked it off with a 30-yard touchdown run for the 27-21 victory. Skattebo had 124 yards rushing and a touchdown. McCarthy will get more starts going forward after looking good against Houston. And Skattebo is unlikely to be benched again anytime soon. Harrison Smith and the Vikings' defense: Smith is one of the more popular Minnesota Vikings players in recent years, and he was celebrated as he appeared to retire at the end of last season. Harrison's retirement didn't last long, as he came back before the season. Then on Sunday he sealed a win with his 40th career interception. The 16-10 win for the Vikings wasn't pretty, and the Indianapolis Colts had a shot to win it at the end on the final drive. But Daniel Jones was pressured and threw downfield, where Smith stepped in front of the receiver for an interception to win the game. HARRISON SMITH GETS THE INT! VIKINGS ARE 6-0 ‼️ pic.twitter.com/stul8J8hWe — NFL (@NFL) October 25, 2026 The Vikings are playing great defense this season. They allowed only 218 yards Sunday. After falling behind early they shut out the Colts in the second half. The Vikings are 6-0 and while there are things to correct after Sunday, particularly on offense, it was a good day to cheer for a franchise legend. Todd Monken: He is getting his first chance to be an NFL head coach at age 60. He's showing that maybe he should have gotten that shot earlier. The Cleveland Browns are 5-2 and one of the best stories in the NFL. They had another dramatic win Sunday, driving down for a field goal after the Tennessee Titans tied it with 58 seconds left. Andre Szmyt hit the game-winning field goal as time expired and the Browns won 27-24. Harold Fannin Jr. with the big catch and run to put the Browns into field goal range! CLEvsTEN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/x27nZZqjK0 — NFL (@NFL) October 25, 2026 Monken took over a situation that seemed terrible due to questions at quarterback. But Deshaun Watson has played well enough, especially with multiple game-winning drives, and the Browns keep winning. That has to be a satisfying start for the rookie head coach. Aaron Rodgers: He used to typically make a few plays a game with his scrambling ability. That was a long time ago. Quarterbacks who are creeping up on their 43rd birthday aren't supposed to be effective anymore, unless they're Tom Brady, and they surely shouldn't be scrambling for first downs to clinch wins. But Rodgers' 8-yard scramble on third-and-6 gave the Pittsburgh Steelers a key first down in a 16-10 win over the New Orleans Saints in the first NFL game in Paris . Still making moves at 42. PITvsNO on NFL Network Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/NjktENol48 — NFL (@NFL) October 25, 2026 More than the play itself, that scramble epitomized how much juice Rodgers still has left in what he has said is his final season. The Steelers are 5-2, putting them in great position to make the playoffs. Rodgers had 212 yards and a touchdown Sunday. While his numbers are a bit down from his fantastic career level, he's still far better than anyone other than Brady has been at his age. If this is it for Rodgers, he's having a good sendoff. LOSERS Aaron Glenn: It was questionable that Glenn got a second season coaching the New York Jets, because his first year was terrible. After Sunday, his time with that job seems to be very close to running out. The Jets lost 28-25 at home to the Miami Dolphins , who were 0-5 coming in. It was a good win for the Dolphins, and the first for Jeff Hafley as an NFL head coach. Miami won't get any 0-17 questions. The Dolphins played like a team that knew it had a shot to beat a poor opponent. And that played out. The Jets didn't play well in any phase. They won their opener against the Titans but have won just once since. The Jets trailed by 11 late on Sunday, got a touchdown and a 2-point conversion, but couldn't stop a fourth-and-1 quarterback sneak just inside of the two-minute warning and the Dolphins ran out the rest of the clock for their first win. The Jets didn't want to fire Glenn after just one season, even though they went 3-14 and there were some alarming signs from Glenn. He replaced most of his staff over the offseason. The results are the same. An embarrassing loss Sunday is a terrible development for Glenn, who might not make it to the end of the season as Jets head coach. It's possible he won't make it to Week 8. The second half Ravens: Baltimore needs to figure out how to play better after halftime. Because it has cost it three wins this season. The Ravens, whose first two losses came after leading 14-6 and 10-0 at halftime, led the Cincinnati Bengals 13-0 after the first half Sunday in a big AFC North showdown. Then their offense, without Lamar Jackson, stopped moving the ball. And their defense, which had pressured Joe Burrow often in the first half, got run off the field in the second half. Burrow had 249 yards and four touchdowns in the second half alone and the Bengals won 35-13 with five unanswered touchdowns in the second half . You can't blame Jackson's absence for that. The Bengals trailed by 13 at halftime but blew the Ravens out so bad in the second half that they pulled Burrow for the final few minutes. Burrow to Ja'Marr for 6, just like clockwork. CINvsBAL on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/VDnK6f5Yjd — NFL (@NFL) October 25, 2026 The Ravens will be division contenders again after Jackson returns. But there's frustration growing with why he was out again with an ankle injury, and there's plenty of other issues that are now nagging at the Ravens. The weird NFC South: The one team that looked like it could be decent from this division trailed the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, who had just one win, 33-6 at halftime. At home. The Carolina Panthers' momentum hit a wall Sunday. The Buccaneers, 1-5 coming into Sunday's game, blew out Carolina 43-13 . It got ugly early. A strip-sack on Bryce Young, who had been playing very well before Sunday, was returned by the Bucs for a touchdown (with a flip into the end zone from 280-pound Calijah Kancey) and a 17-0 lead. Young had just 163 yards, two interceptions and a lost fumble. When the Panthers finally scored, their extra point was blocked and returned by Tampa Bay for 2 points. The Panthers played a sloppy game all around. Baker Mayfield was back but the Buccaneers hardly needed him. Mayfield had just 64 yards passing but the Panthers were imploding on the other side of the field. It's hard to say a 2-5 team is back in a division race, but it's not like the NFC South has any good teams, it appears. That's nothing new.

stories.title: 49ers lose to the Falcons in a game full of turnovers and mistakes
stories.summary: The 49ers could not get out of their own way against the Falcons
stories.detailText: (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers offense wasted no time scoring, marching 64 yards in just over five minutes on 10 plays for a touchdown to start the game. Christian McCaffrey gained 16 and 24 yards on the drive. The Falcons took the ensuing kickoff 61 yards. Fred Warner made a phenomenal third-down tackle, bringing down Bijan Robinson in the backfield for a three-yard loss. The Falcons settled for a field goal, making it 7-3. The Niners’ second drive stalled after Connor Colby surrendered a sack. This came after George Kittle picked up 17 yards on 3rd and 4. The Falcons also went three-and-out on a penalty. Christian McCaffrey missed the next drive. He ran up and down the sideline, trying to get loose. According to the broadcast, McCaffrey was dealing with a thigh injury. On the first drive without McCaffrey, rookie Kaelon Black ran for 15, 7, and a 30-yard touchdown to give the 49ers a 14-3 lead. The drive took 1:41 off the clock and came in just four plays. The Falcons answered with a touchdown on a 10-play, 68-yard drive. Atlanta’s kicker missed the extra point, making it 14-9. Jacob Cowing took a 10-yard reverse for a first down. Jordan James’ first carry of the game was a fumble that safety Xavier Watts appeared to recover, but Luke Farrell wrestled it away. Black fumbled on the second consecutive play. The 49ers weren’t fortunate enough to recover this one. The giveaway came on Atlanta’s 28-yard line on 2nd and 1. The Niners were bound to put points on the board. The Falcons took the rest of the first half with their next possession. They went to draw the Niners offsides with 29 seconds remaining. On 4th and 4, Osa Odighizuwa jumped offsides. Atlanta got a field goal out of the drive. The Falcons began the third quarter with the football. They did whatever they wanted on the drive, gaining 8, 10, and 12 yards before Michael Penix found Kyle Pitts for a 5-yard touchdown. That gave Atlanta a 19-14 lead. Jordan Watkins made the first wide receiver catch with just under nine minutes remaining in the third quarter. Watkins laid out for an impressive reception. Purdy kept the drive alive when there wasn’t anything there after scrambling. Kittle picked up a big chunk, then Farrell followed suit. But Purdy got a little too greedy on his next scramble. Instead of throwing the ball into the stands, he cut it close, and the Falcons intercepted it. This turnover came on Atlanta’s 25, squandering another scoring opportunity. The secondary continued to struggle. On 2nd and 20, Jack Jones committed an illegal contact penalty. On 3rd down, Bijan Robinson was uncovered on a coverage bust involving Dre Greenlaw, Jones, and Deommodore Lenoir. It looked like Greenlaw was in the wrong. Jones committed pass interference on 3rd and 8. James Thompson was offside on 3rd and 2, on a play where it looked like the 49ers got hosed by the substitution rule. Penix found Drake London down the seam on the next play, giving the Falcons a commanding 26-14 lead. The 49ers. gave Atlanta multiple first downs via penalty on the drive. The 49ers were aggressive on their next drive. Purdy found Watkins for 35 yards, but Connor Colby’s hold negated a 10-yard run by McCaffrey on the next play. Purdy threw a seed to Watkins in the end zone with perfect placement. But for the second time in the game, Watkins couldn’t secure the catch through the ground. An incomplete pass and a sack meant the 49ers would come away with no points on the drive. The Falcons helped the defense out on the next drive, after snapping the ball over Penix’s head. The 49ers got the ball back in 1:57. Purdy found Jacob Cowing for an 18-yard gain on the next drive. Cowing drew a defensive holding penalty two plays later. A 15-yard facemask by the Falcons pushed the ball deeper into Falcons territory. Kittle gained 11 yards to put the Niners at the 11. Purdy found McCaffrey just shy of the goal line, then threw to Kyle Juszczyk to make it a one-possession game, 26-20, after Eddy Pineiro missed the extra point. The defense forced a quick three-and-out. Atlanta shanked the punt. The offense had great field position, plenty of time, and all three timeouts. On 3rd and 4, Brandin Cooks flinched. That made it 3rd and 9. An underneath linebacker intercepted Purdy’s pass, sealing the game for the Falcons. That was San Francisco’s third turnover. Pineiro’s miss loomed large, as a Falcons field goal could make it a two-possession game. The Falcons tacked on a field goal to make it 29-20, all but ending the game. Fittingly, Kittle fumbled as the Niners were driving to make it a one-possession game.

teamStories.detailText: Photo by Katelyn Mulcahy/Getty Images | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams (2-4) travel to take on the Las Vegas Raiders (3-3) in Week 7 of the NFL season. teamStories.summary: Nacua's availability is a huge relief for a Rams squad that has been decimated by injuries over the past week.
teamStories.detailText: Puka Nacua is officially active for the Los Angeles Rams ' Week 7 matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday, Oct. 25, the team announced pregame. Nacua had been listed as questionable with a calf injury since leaving Thursday's practice early. He did not practice on Friday, after which head coach Sean McVay told reporters he would be a pregame decision. As for what caused the injury, that's still a mystery. "I don't think he knows exactly when it occurred," McVay said. "You look at it and there's a little minor thing in there. Felt it where he wasn't able to have some of the power and full explosion. Just noticed it, but I don't think he was aware of any sort of specific play that led to it." There was optimism that the fourth-year receiver would be able to play, however, and his availability is a huge break for a Rams offense that has been in dire need of good news – especially in the receivers room. Davante Adams ruptured his right hamstring on the final drive of last week's loss to the Arizona Cardinals and will be out for 6-10 weeks. Tight end Terrance Ferguson has also been on the IR since suffering a medial ankle sprain in Week 3. Nacua already missed two games earlier this year with a hip/groin injury but has been productive since returning three weeks ago with 417 yards on 37 catches in four games played this season. Not losing his presence is a win in and of itself for the Rams. "Whether you're talking about (Adams), whether you're talking about Puka, you don't ever ask anybody to replace those guys," McVay told reporters on Friday. "They're unique guys that have meant so much to us. I want those players to be their best selves whether that's (Konata Mumpfield), whether that's Tutu (Atwell), whether that's (Jordan Whittington), whether that's C.J. Daniels."
